376:     /// WLAST: `warning` is the last statement in a function (may need `error` instead).
377:     fn check_wlast(&self, tree: &tree_sitter::Tree, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
378:         if !self.is_check_enabled("WLAST") {
379:             return Vec::new();
380:         }
381: 
382:         let meta = FileMeta::build(tree, source);
383:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
384: 
385:         for func in &meta.functions {
386:             self.check_wlast_in_range(
387:                 tree.root_node(),
388:                 source,
389:                 func.byte_range.clone(),
390:                 &mut diagnostics,
391:             );
392:         }
393:         for func in &meta.local_functions {
394:             self.check_wlast_in_range(
395:                 tree.root_node(),
396:                 source,
397:                 func.byte_range.clone(),
398:                 &mut diagnostics,
399:             );
400:         }
401: 
402:         diagnostics
403:     }

405:     /// Helper: check if the last statement in a byte range is a `warning()` call.
406:     fn check_wlast_in_range(
407:         &self,
408:         root: Node,
409:         source: &str,
410:         range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
411:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
412:     ) {
413:         // Find the function_definition node covering this range.
414:         let func_node = find_node_in_range(root, &range);
415:         let func_node = match func_node {
416:             Some(n) if n.kind() == "function_definition" => n,
417:             _ => return,
418:         };
419: 
420:         // Get the block child (function body).
421:         let block = match find_child_of_kind(func_node, "block") {
422:             Some(b) => b,
423:             None => return,
424:         };
425: 
426:         // Find the last named non-`end` child.
427:         let last_stmt = last_named_child_not_end(block);
428:         let last_stmt = match last_stmt {
429:             Some(s) => s,
430:             None => return,
431:         };
432: 
433:         // Check if it's a warning() call.
434:         if last_stmt.kind() != "function_call" {
435:             return;
436:         }
437:         let name = get_function_call_name(last_stmt, source);
438:         if name != Some("warning") {
439:             return;
440:         }
441: 
442:         let pos = last_stmt.start_position();
443:         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
444:             rule_id: "WLAST",
445:             message: "WARNING('') does not reset the warning state. Use LASTWARN('') instead."
446:                 .to_string(),
447:             severity: Severity::Warning,
448:             byte_range: last_stmt.start_byte()..last_stmt.end_byte(),
449:             line: pos.row + 1,
450:             column: pos.column + 1,
451:             fix: None,
452:         });
453:     }

499:     /// PFIIN / PFOUS / PFTUSW / PFUIXW: PARFOR loop data-flow checks.
500:     ///
501:     /// Uses the symbol table with byte-range comparisons because the symbol
502:     /// table has no per-parfor scope.
503:     fn check_parfor_file_level(&self, tree: &tree_sitter::Tree, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
504:         let any_enabled = self.is_check_enabled("PFIIN")
505:             || self.is_check_enabled("PFOUS")
506:             || self.is_check_enabled("PFTUSW")
507:             || self.is_check_enabled("PFUIXW");
508:         if !any_enabled {
509:             return Vec::new();
510:         }
511: 
512:         let sym = SymbolTable::build(tree, source);
513:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
514:         let parfors = collect_parfor_nodes(tree.root_node(), source);
515: 
516:         for parfor in &parfors {
517:             let idx_var = extract_parfor_index_var(*parfor, source);
518:             let body = find_child_of_kind(*parfor, "block");
519: 
520:             // PFIIN: input variable read in the body but never initialized
521:             // before the loop and not assigned inside the loop.
522:             if self.is_check_enabled("PFIIN") {
523:                 if let Some(body_node) = body {
524:                     let mut skip = std::collections::HashSet::new();
525:                     if let Some(ref idx) = idx_var {
526:                         skip.insert(idx.clone());
527:                     }
528:                     let reads = collect_parfor_body_reads(body_node, source, &skip);
529:                     for (name, read_node) in reads {
530:                         if is_defined_before_parfor(&sym, &name, parfor.start_byte())
531:                             || is_assigned_in_body(body_node, &name, source)
532:                         {
533:                             continue;
534:                         }
535:                         let pos = read_node.start_position();
536:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
537:                             rule_id: "PFIIN",
538:                             message: format!(
539:                                 "The input variable {name} should be initialized before the PARFOR loop."
540:                             ),
541:                             severity: Severity::Warning,
542:                             byte_range: read_node.start_byte()..read_node.end_byte(),
543:                             line: pos.row + 1,
544:                             column: pos.column + 1,
545:                             fix: None,
546:                         });
547:                     }
548:                 }
549:             }
550: 
551:             // PFOUS / PFTUSW: simple-identifier assignments in the body and
552:             // whether the variable is used after the loop.
553:             let need_assignments =
554:                 self.is_check_enabled("PFOUS") || self.is_check_enabled("PFTUSW");
555:             if need_assignments {
556:                 if let Some(body_node) = body {
557:                     let assigned = collect_simple_lhs_assignments(body_node, source);
558:                     for (name, lhs_node) in assigned {
559:                         if idx_var.as_deref() == Some(name.as_str()) {
560:                             continue;
561:                         }
562:                         let uses = uses_after_parfor(&sym, &name, parfor.end_byte(), tree, false);
563:                         if self.is_check_enabled("PFOUS") && uses.is_empty() {
564:                             let pos = lhs_node.start_position();
565:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
566:                                 rule_id: "PFOUS",
567:                                 message: format!(
568:                                     "The output variable {name} might not be used after the PARFOR loop."
569:                                 ),
570:                                 severity: Severity::Warning,
571:                                 byte_range: lhs_node.start_byte()..lhs_node.end_byte(),
572:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
573:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
574:                                 fix: None,
575:                             });
576:                         }
577:                         if self.is_check_enabled("PFTUSW") {
578:                             if let Some(line) = uses.first() {
579:                                 let pos = lhs_node.start_position();
580:                                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
581:                                     rule_id: "PFTUSW",
582:                                     message: format!(
583:                                         "The temporary variable {name} might be used after the PARFOR loop on line {line}. The value set on this line is not available after the loop."
584:                                     ),
585:                                     severity: Severity::Warning,
586:                                     byte_range: lhs_node.start_byte()..lhs_node.end_byte(),
587:                                     line: pos.row + 1,
588:                                     column: pos.column + 1,
589:                                     fix: None,
590:                                 });
591:                             }
592:                         }
593:                     }
594:                 }
595:             }
596: 
597:             // PFUIXW: index variable used after the loop.
598:             if self.is_check_enabled("PFUIXW") {
599:                 if let Some(ref idx) = idx_var {
600:                     let uses = uses_after_parfor(&sym, idx, parfor.end_byte(), tree, true);
601:                     if let Some(line) = uses.first() {
602:                         let idx_node = find_parfor_index_identifier(*parfor);
603:                         let target = idx_node.unwrap_or(*parfor);
604:                         let pos = target.start_position();
605:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
606:                             rule_id: "PFUIXW",
607:                             message: format!(
608:                                 "The index variable {idx} might be used after the PARFOR loop on line {line}. The value set on this line is not available after the loop."
609:                             ),
610:                             severity: Severity::Warning,
611:                             byte_range: target.start_byte()..target.end_byte(),
612:                             line: pos.row + 1,
613:                             column: pos.column + 1,
614:                             fix: None,
615:                         });
616:                     }
617:                 }
618:             }
619:         }
620: 
621:         diagnostics
622:     }

624:     /// Shared COMPNOP/COMPNOT logic: extract the `(call, literal, operator)`
625:     /// triple from a `comparison_operator` node when exactly one operand is a
626:     /// `function_call` and the other is the `true`/`false` literal.
627:     pub(crate) fn comparison_with_literal<'a>(
628:         &self,
629:         node: Node<'a>,
630:         source: &'a str,
631:     ) -> Option<(Node<'a>, Node<'a>, String)> {
632:         let lhs = node.child(0)?;
633:         let rhs = node.child(2)?;
634:         let op = find_operator_text(node, source);
635: 
636:         let (call_node, literal_node) = match (lhs.kind(), rhs.kind()) {
637:             ("function_call", "identifier") => (lhs, rhs),
638:             ("identifier", "function_call") => (rhs, lhs),
639:             _ => return None,
640:         };
641:         let literal = node_text(literal_node, source).trim();
642:         if literal == "true" || literal == "false" {
643:             Some((call_node, literal_node, op))
644:         } else {
645:             None
646:         }
647:     }
648: }

1: //! Logical-usage checks (BDLGI, BDLOG1, BDLOG2, BDSCA, BDSCI).
2: //!
3: //! These checks reason about variables used in boolean contexts (bare `if x` /
4: //! `while x` conditions) and short-circuit operators. They consume the
5: //! conservative [`TypeEnv`] built by `crate::analysis::typing` and only fire
6: //! on provable cases:
7: //!
8: //! - BDLGI  — the condition variable was assigned from an arithmetic operator.
9: //! - BDLOG1 — the condition variable is logical but not scalar.
10: //! - BDLOG2 — the condition value is scalar but not provably logical.
11: //! - BDSCA  — a `&&` / `||` operand is a non-scalar logical array.
12: //! - BDSCI  — the condition variable was assigned from an array-producing
13: //!   expression (`a:b`, `[...]`, `{...}`).
14: //!
15: //! All diagnostics are `Severity::Warning` and gated on `disabled_checks`.
16: 
17: use std::collections::HashMap;
18:

20: use crate::analysis::typing::{TypeEnv, TypeKind};

22: /// Per-name assignment classifications collected by scanning every assignment
23: /// in the file. Each map records the classification of the *latest* assignment
24: /// to the name, mirroring the type environment's last-assignment-wins rule.
25: struct AssignmentClasses {
26:     /// Names whose latest assignment RHS is an arithmetic operator.
27:     arith: HashMap<String, bool>,
28:     /// Names whose latest assignment RHS is provably non-scalar.
29:     nonscalar: HashMap<String, bool>,
30:     /// Names whose latest assignment RHS is a number literal.
31:     scalar_literal: HashMap<String, bool>,
32: }
33: 
34: impl GoodPracticesEngine {
35:     /// BDLGI / BDLOG1 / BDLOG2 / BDSCA / BDSCI: file-level logical-usage
36:     /// checks driven by the type environment.
37:     pub(crate) fn check_logical_usage(
38:         &self,
39:         tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
40:         source: &str,
41:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
42:         let any_enabled = self.is_check_enabled("BDLGI")
43:             || self.is_check_enabled("BDLOG1")
44:             || self.is_check_enabled("BDLOG2")
45:             || self.is_check_enabled("BDSCA")
46:             || self.is_check_enabled("BDSCI");
47:         if !any_enabled {
48:             return Vec::new();
49:         }
50: 
51:         let env = TypeEnv::build(tree, source);
52:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
53: 
54:         // ---- Pass 1: classify every simple-identifier assignment ----------
55:         // Last assignment wins, mirroring the TypeEnv's semantics.
56:         let mut classes = AssignmentClasses {
57:             arith: HashMap::new(),
58:             nonscalar: HashMap::new(),
59:             scalar_literal: HashMap::new(),
60:         };
61:         let mut assignments = Vec::new();
62:         collect_nodes_of_kind(tree.root_node(), "assignment", &mut assignments);
63:         for assign in assignments {
64:             let Some(lhs) = assign.child_by_field_name("left") else {
65:                 continue;
66:             };
67:             if lhs.kind() != "identifier" {
68:                 continue;
69:             }
70:             let name = node_text(lhs, source).to_string();
71:             let Some(rhs) = assign.child_by_field_name("right") else {
72:                 continue;
73:             };
74:             classes
75:                 .arith
76:                 .insert(name.clone(), is_arithmetic_rhs(rhs, source));
77:             classes
78:                 .nonscalar
79:                 .insert(name.clone(), is_nonscalar_rhs(rhs, source));
80:             classes
81:                 .scalar_literal
82:                 .insert(name.clone(), rhs.kind() == "number");
83:         }
84: 
85:         // ---- Pass 2: walk if/while/elseif/switch condition expressions ----
86:         let mut conditions = Vec::new();
87:         collect_condition_expressions(tree.root_node(), &mut conditions);
88:         for (cond, is_if_while) in conditions {
89:             check_bare_condition(
90:                 cond,
91:                 is_if_while,
92:                 &env,
93:                 &classes,
94:                 source,
95:                 self,
96:                 &mut diagnostics,
97:             );
98:         }
99: 
100:         // ---- Pass 3: BDSCA — `&&`/`||` with a non-scalar logical operand ---
101:         if self.is_check_enabled("BDSCA") {
102:             collect_bdsca(tree.root_node(), &env, source, &mut diagnostics);
103:         }
104: 
105:         diagnostics
106:     }
107: }

109: /// Whether an assignment RHS produces a non-logical (arithmetic) value.
110: ///
111: /// Only `binary_operator` nodes whose operator is arithmetic (`+ - * / ^ \`
112: /// and their element-wise forms) qualify; comparisons, element-wise boolean
113: /// `&`/`|`, and short-circuit `&&`/`||` do not.
114: fn is_arithmetic_rhs(rhs: Node, source: &str) -> bool {
115:     if rhs.kind() != "binary_operator" {
116:         return false;
117:     }
118:     let op = find_operator_text(rhs, source);
119:     !op.is_empty() && op.chars().all(|c| "+-*/^\\.".contains(c))
120: }
121: 
122: /// Whether an assignment RHS is provably non-scalar: a colon range, or a
123: /// matrix/cell literal with more than one element.
124: fn is_nonscalar_rhs(rhs: Node, _source: &str) -> bool {
125:     match rhs.kind() {
126:         "range" => true,
127:         "matrix" | "cell" => !array_literal_is_scalar(rhs),
128:         _ => false,
129:     }
130: }

132: /// Whether a `matrix` / `cell` literal contains exactly one element.
133: fn array_literal_is_scalar(node: Node) -> bool {
134:     let mut count = 0usize;
135:     let mut stack = vec![node];
136:     while let Some(n) = stack.pop() {
137:         let mut cursor = n.walk();
138:         for child in n.children(&mut cursor) {
139:             if !child.is_named() {
140:                 continue;
141:             }
142:             match child.kind() {
143:                 "row" | "array" => stack.push(child),
144:                 "number" | "string" | "identifier" | "true" | "false" | "number_constant"
145:                 | "unary_operator" | "binary_operator" | "range" | "function_call" => {
146:                     count += 1;
147:                 }
148:                 _ => stack.push(child),
149:             }
150:         }
151:     }
152:     count == 1
153: }

155: /// Collect `(condition, is_if_while)` pairs: the condition of every
156: /// `if_statement`, `while_statement` and `elseif_clause`, plus the switch
157: /// expression of every `switch_statement` (with `is_if_while == false`).
158: fn collect_condition_expressions<'a>(node: Node<'a>, out: &mut Vec<(Node<'a>, bool)>) {
159:     match node.kind() {
160:         "if_statement" | "while_statement" | "elseif_clause" => {
161:             if let Some(cond) = first_named_child(node) {
162:                 out.push((cond, true));
163:             }
164:         }
165:         "switch_statement" => {
166:             if let Some(expr) = first_named_child(node) {
167:                 out.push((expr, false));
168:             }
169:         }
170:         _ => {}
171:     }
172:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
173:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
174:         if child.is_named() {
175:             collect_condition_expressions(child, out);
176:         }
177:     }
178: }

180: /// Apply the bare-condition checks (BDLGI / BDLOG1 / BDLOG2 / BDSCI) to a
181: /// condition expression. Parentheses around a simple value are unwrapped so
182: /// `if (x)` behaves like `if x`.
183: fn check_bare_condition(
184:     cond: Node,
185:     is_if_while: bool,
186:     env: &TypeEnv,
187:     classes: &AssignmentClasses,
188:     source: &str,
189:     eng: &GoodPracticesEngine,
190:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
191: ) {
192:     if !is_if_while {
193:         return;
194:     }
195:     let mut value = cond;
196:     while value.kind() == "parenthesis" || value.kind() == "parenthesized_expression" {
197:         match first_named_child(value) {
198:             Some(inner) => value = inner,
199:             None => return,
200:         }
201:     }
202:     let pos = value.start_position();
203:     match value.kind() {
204:         "identifier" => {
205:             let name = node_text(value, source);
206:             let info = env.type_of(name);
207: 
208:             if eng.is_check_enabled("BDLGI")
209:                 && classes.arith.get(name) == Some(&true)
210:                 && info.kind != TypeKind::Logical
211:             {
212:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
213:                     rule_id: "BDLGI",
214:                     message: "Variable might be set by a nonlogical operator.".to_string(),
215:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
216:                     byte_range: value.start_byte()..value.end_byte(),
217:                     line: pos.row + 1,
218:                     column: pos.column + 1,
219:                     fix: None,
220:                 });
221:             }
222: 
223:             if eng.is_check_enabled("BDLOG1") && info.kind == TypeKind::Logical && !info.scalar {
224:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
225:                     rule_id: "BDLOG1",
226:                     message: "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. \
227:                               Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar."
228:                         .to_string(),
229:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
230:                     byte_range: value.start_byte()..value.end_byte(),
231:                     line: pos.row + 1,
232:                     column: pos.column + 1,
233:                     fix: None,
234:                 });
235:             }
236: 
237:             if eng.is_check_enabled("BDLOG2")
238:                 && info.kind != TypeKind::Logical
239:                 && (info.scalar || classes.scalar_literal.get(name) == Some(&true))
240:             {
241:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
242:                     rule_id: "BDLOG2",
243:                     message: "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. \
244:                               Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar, or \
245:                               compare the scalar value to 0."
246:                         .to_string(),
247:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
248:                     byte_range: value.start_byte()..value.end_byte(),
249:                     line: pos.row + 1,
250:                     column: pos.column + 1,
251:                     fix: None,
252:                 });
253:             }

255:             if eng.is_check_enabled("BDSCI") && classes.nonscalar.get(name) == Some(&true) {
256:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {

258:                     message: "Variable might be set by a nonscalar operator.".to_string(),
259:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
260:                     byte_range: value.start_byte()..value.end_byte(),
261:                     line: pos.row + 1,
262:                     column: pos.column + 1,

264:                 });

268:             if eng.is_check_enabled("BDLOG2") {

271:                     message: "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. \
272:                               Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar, or \

276:                     byte_range: value.start_byte()..value.end_byte(),

289: fn collect_bdsca(node: Node, env: &TypeEnv, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
290:     if node.kind() == "boolean_operator" || node.kind() == "boolean_operator_short" {
291:         let op = find_operator_text(node, source);

293:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
294:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
295:             if !child.is_named() || child.kind() != "identifier" {
296:                 continue;
297:             }
298:             let name = node_text(child, source);
299:             let info = env.type_of(name);
300:             if info.kind != TypeKind::Logical || info.scalar {
301:                 continue;
302:             }
303:             let pos = node.start_position();
304:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
305:                 rule_id: "BDSCA",

307:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
308:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
309:                 line: pos.row + 1,
310:                 column: pos.column + 1,
311:                 fix: None,
312:             });

317:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
318:         if child.is_named() {

1383: /// Emit use-of-global diagnostics for a body node (PFGV / SPGV).
1384: ///
1385: /// When `skip_writes` is true, assignment LHS identifiers are excluded
1386: /// (they are handled by the separate PFGP check).
1387: pub(crate) fn collect_global_use_diagnostics<'a>(
1388:     body: Node<'a>,
1389:     source: &str,
1390:     globals: &std::collections::HashSet<String>,
1391:     rule_id: &'static str,
1392:     skip_writes: bool,
1393: ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
1394:     let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
1395:     let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
1396:     let mut identifiers = Vec::new();
1397:     collect_nodes_of_kind(body, "identifier", &mut identifiers);
1398:     for id in identifiers {
1399:         let name = node_text(id, source).to_string();
1400:         if !globals.contains(&name) {
1401:             continue;
1402:         }
1403:         if let Some(parent) = id.parent() {
1404:             match parent.kind() {
1405:                 "global_operator" | "persistent_operator" => continue,
1406:                 "assignment" => {
1407:                     if skip_writes
1408:                         && parent
1409:                             .child_by_field_name("left")
1410:                             .map(|l| l.id() == id.id())
1411:                             .unwrap_or(false)
1412:                     {
1413:                         continue;
1414:                     }
1415:                 }
1416:                 "field_expression" => {
1417:                     if parent
1418:                         .child_by_field_name("field")
1419:                         .map(|f| f.id() == id.id())
1420:                         .unwrap_or(false)
1421:                     {
1422:                         continue;
1423:                     }
1424:                 }
1425:                 _ => {}
1426:             }
1427:         }
1428:         if !seen.insert(name.clone()) {
1429:             continue;
1430:         }
1431:         let pos = id.start_position();
1432:         let message = if rule_id == "PFGV" {
1433:             format!("Avoid using GLOBAL variable {name} in a PARFOR loop.")
1434:         } else {
1435:             format!(
1436:                 "Using the GLOBAL or PERSISTENT variable {name} in an SPMD block might fail because it is accessed on a worker machine."
1437:             )
1438:         };
1439:         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1440:             rule_id,
1441:             message,
1442:             severity: Severity::Warning,
1443:             byte_range: id.start_byte()..id.end_byte(),
1444:             line: pos.row + 1,
1445:             column: pos.column + 1,
1446:             fix: None,
1447:         });
1448:     }
1449:     diagnostics
1450: }

1452: /// Collect plain-identifier reads inside a parfor body (for PFIIN).
1453: ///
1454: /// Function-call names, assignment LHS writes, field names, and declarations
1455: /// are excluded; only genuine variable reads are returned, deduplicated by name.
1456: pub(crate) fn collect_parfor_body_reads<'a>(
1457:     node: Node<'a>,
1458:     source: &str,
1459:     skip: &std::collections::HashSet<String>,
1460: ) -> Vec<(String, Node<'a>)> {
1461:     let mut out = Vec::new();
1462:     let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
1463:     let mut identifiers = Vec::new();
1464:     collect_nodes_of_kind(node, "identifier", &mut identifiers);
1465:     for id in identifiers {
1466:         let name = node_text(id, source).to_string();
1467:         if skip.contains(&name) {
1468:             continue;
1469:         }
1470:         if let Some(parent) = id.parent() {
1471:             match parent.kind() {
1472:                 "function_call" => {
1473:                     if parent
1474:                         .child_by_field_name("name")
1475:                         .map(|n| n.id() == id.id())
1476:                         .unwrap_or(false)
1477:                     {
1478:                         continue;
1479:                     }
1480:                 }
1481:                 "assignment" => {
1482:                     if parent
1483:                         .child_by_field_name("left")
1484:                         .map(|l| l.id() == id.id())
1485:                         .unwrap_or(false)
1486:                     {
1487:                         continue;
1488:                     }
1489:                 }
1490:                 "global_operator" | "persistent_operator" => continue,
1491:                 "field_expression" => {
1492:                     if parent
1493:                         .child_by_field_name("field")
1494:                         .map(|f| f.id() == id.id())
1495:                         .unwrap_or(false)
1496:                     {
1497:                         continue;
1498:                     }
1499:                 }
1500:                 "iterator" => continue,
1501:                 _ => {}
1502:             }
1503:         }
1504:         if seen.insert(name.clone()) {
1505:             out.push((name, id));
1506:         }
1507:     }
1508:     out
1509: }

1554: /// Collect lines where a variable is used after a byte offset.
1555: ///
1556: /// When `exclude_loops` is true, uses inside any enclosing `for_statement`
1557: /// are ignored (the variable is re-bound by a subsequent loop).
1558: pub(crate) fn uses_after_parfor(
1559:     sym: &SymbolTable,
1560:     name: &str,
1561:     after: usize,
1562:     tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
1563:     exclude_loops: bool,
1564: ) -> Vec<usize> {
1565:     let mut lines = Vec::new();
1566:     for scope in &sym.scopes {
1567:         for u in &scope.uses {
1568:             if u.name != name || u.byte_range.start < after {
1569:                 continue;
1570:             }
1571:             if exclude_loops {
1572:                 if let Some(n) = tree
1573:                     .root_node()
1574:                     .descendant_for_byte_range(u.byte_range.start, u.byte_range.end)
1575:                 {
1576:                     if is_inside_loop(n) {
1577:                         continue;
1578:                     }
1579:                 }
1580:             }
1581:             lines.push(u.line);
1582:         }
1583:     }
1584:     lines.sort_unstable();
1585:     lines.dedup();
1586:     lines
1587: }

1616: /// Count `printf`-style format specifiers in a format string (for CTPCT).
1617: ///
1618: /// Counts `%` followed by a conversion character. Escaped `%%`, `%*` width
1619: /// specifiers, and `%n$` positional specifiers are not counted.
1620: pub(crate) fn count_format_specifiers(fmt: &str) -> usize {
1621:     let chars: Vec<char> = fmt.chars().collect();
1622:     let mut count = 0;
1623:     let mut i = 0;
1624:     while i < chars.len() {
1625:         if chars[i] != '%' {
1626:             i += 1;
1627:             continue;
1628:         }
1629:         let j = i + 1;
1630:         if j >= chars.len() {
1631:             break;
1632:         }
1633:         if chars[j] == '%' {
1634:             i = j + 1;
1635:             continue;
1636:         }
1637:         if chars[j] == '*' {
1638:             let mut k = j + 1;
1639:             while k < chars.len() && !chars[k].is_ascii_alphabetic() {
1640:                 k += 1;
1641:             }
1642:             i = k + 1;
1643:             continue;
1644:         }
1645:         let mut k = j;
1646:         while k < chars.len() && chars[k].is_ascii_digit() {
1647:             k += 1;
1648:         }
1649:         if k < chars.len() && chars[k] == '$' {
1650:             let mut m = k + 1;
1651:             while m < chars.len() && !chars[m].is_ascii_alphabetic() {
1652:                 m += 1;
1653:             }
1654:             i = m + 1;
1655:             continue;
1656:         }
1657:         while k < chars.len() && "-+ #0".contains(chars[k]) {
1658:             k += 1;
1659:         }
1660:         while k < chars.len() && chars[k].is_ascii_digit() {
1661:             k += 1;
1662:         }
1663:         if k < chars.len() && chars[k] == '.' {
1664:             k += 1;
1665:             while k < chars.len() && chars[k].is_ascii_digit() {
1666:                 k += 1;
1667:             }
1668:         }
1669:         if k < chars.len() && chars[k].is_ascii_alphabetic() {
1670:             count += 1;
1671:             i = k + 1;
1672:         } else {
1673:             i = j;
1674:         }
1675:     }
1676:     count
1677: }

1679: /// Collect assignments to `var_name` inside a loop body, without descending
1680: /// into nested function definitions or anonymous functions (for FXSET).
1681: pub(crate) fn collect_loop_assignments(
1682:     node: Node,
1683:     var_name: &str,
1684:     source: &str,
1685:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,

1687:     if node.kind() == "function_definition" || node.kind() == "lambda" {
1688:         return;

1690:     if node.kind() == "assignment" {
1691:         if let Some(left) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
1692:             if left.kind() == "identifier" && node_text(left, source) == var_name {
1693:                 let pos = node.start_position();
1694:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1695:                     rule_id: "FXSET",
1696:                     message: format!("Loop index {var_name} is changed inside of a FOR loop."),
1697:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
1698:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1699:                     line: pos.row + 1,
1700:                     column: pos.column + 1,
1701:                     fix: None,
1702:                 });
1703:             }
1704:         }
1705:     }
1706:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
1707:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {

1759:     class_node: Node<'a>,
1760:     index: usize,

1829: /// Recursively find the first descendant of a node with the given kind.
1830: #[cfg(test)]
1831: pub(crate) fn find_descendant_of_kind<'a>(node: Node<'a>, kind: &str) -> Option<Node<'a>> {
1832:     if node.kind() == kind {
1833:         return Some(node);
1834:     }
1835:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
1836:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1837:         if let Some(found) = find_descendant_of_kind(child, kind) {
1838:             return Some(found);
1839:         }
1840:     }
1841:     None
1842: }

1844: /// Find all descendant nodes of the given kind.
1845: #[cfg(test)]
1846: pub(crate) fn all_descendants_of_kind<'a>(node: Node<'a>, kind: &str) -> Vec<Node<'a>> {
1847:     let mut result = Vec::new();
1848:     if node.kind() == kind {
1849:         result.push(node);
1850:     }
1851:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
1852:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1853:         result.extend(all_descendants_of_kind(child, kind));
1854:     }
1855:     result

210: /// Extract the source text covered by a node.
211: fn node_text<'a>(node: Node, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
212:     &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
213: }

215: /// Extract attributes from an `attributes` node.
216: ///
217: /// Each `attribute` child represents a single attribute entry.
218: /// Attributes can be:
219: /// - Bare: `Sealed` (value is `None`, treated as `true`)
220: /// - Valued: `Access = private`
221: /// - Negated: `~Hidden` (negated flag set)
222: fn extract_attributes(attrs_node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<AttributeMeta> {
223:     let mut attrs = Vec::new();
224:     let mut cursor = attrs_node.walk();
225: 
226:     for child in attrs_node.children(&mut cursor) {
227:         if child.kind() != "attribute" {
228:             continue;
229:         }
230: 
231:         let text = node_text(child, source).trim();
232:         let negated = text.starts_with('~');
233: 
234:         // Find the attribute name — first identifier child.
235:         let name = find_first_child_of_kind(child, "identifier")
236:             .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string())
237:             .unwrap_or_default();
238: 
239:         if name.is_empty() {
240:             continue;
241:         }
242: 
243:         // Look for `= value` portion.  The value is everything after the `=`.
244:         // In the grammar an attribute with a value has the identifier, then `=`, then
245:         // one or more value children (which may be identifiers, strings, etc.).
246:         let value = extract_attribute_value(child, source);
247: 
248:         attrs.push(AttributeMeta {
249:             name,
250:             value,
251:             negated,
252:         });
253:     }
254: 
255:     attrs
256: }
257: 
258: /// Extract the value portion of an `attribute` node (everything after `=`).
259: ///
260: /// Returns `None` if no `=` is present (bare attribute).
261: fn extract_attribute_value(attr_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<String> {
262:     let mut found_eq = false;
263:     let mut cursor = attr_node.walk();
264: 
265:     for child in attr_node.children(&mut cursor) {
266:         let kind = child.kind();
267:         let text = node_text(child, source);
268: 
269:         if text == "=" {
270:             found_eq = true;
271:             continue;
272:         }
273: 
274:         if found_eq && kind != "=" {
275:             // Capture the first meaningful token after `=` as the value.
276:             return Some(text.trim().to_string());
277:         }
278:     }
279: 
280:     None
281: }

283: /// Find the first child of a node with the given kind.
284: fn find_first_child_of_kind<'a>(node: Node<'a>, kind: &str) -> Option<Node<'a>> {
285:     let child_count = node.child_count();
286:     for i in 0..child_count {
287:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
288:             if child.kind() == kind {
289:                 return Some(child);
290:             }
291:         }
292:     }
293:     None
294: }

300: /// Build the full function name, including `set.` or `get.` prefix if present.
301: ///
302: /// In tree-sitter-matlab, `function set.Value(...)` produces:
303: /// - a child node with kind `set.`
304: /// - the `name` field pointing to the `identifier` node `Value`
305: ///
306: /// This function checks for that prefix and prepends it to the base name.
307: fn build_function_name(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<String> {
308:     let name_node = func_node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
309:     let base_name = node_text(name_node, source);
310: 
311:     // Check for `set.` or `get.` prefix child.
312:     let child_count = func_node.child_count();
313:     for i in 0..child_count {
314:         if let Some(child) = func_node.child(i) {
315:             let kind = child.kind();
316:             if kind == "set." || kind == "get." {
317:                 return Some(format!("{}{}", kind, base_name));
318:             }
319:         }
320:     }
321: 
322:     Some(base_name.to_string())
323: }

325: /// Extract metadata from a `function_definition` node.
326: fn extract_function_meta(
327:     node: Node,
328:     source: &str,
329:     class_name: Option<&str>,
330:     is_method: bool,
331:     method_attributes: &[AttributeMeta],
332:     is_abstract: bool,
333: ) -> Option<FunctionMeta> {
334:     let name = build_function_name(node, source)?;
335: 
336:     let inputs = extract_function_inputs(node, source);
337:     let outputs = extract_function_outputs(node, source);
338: 
339:     let is_constructor = class_name.is_some_and(|cn| cn == name);
340:     let is_setter = name.starts_with("set.");
341:     let is_getter = name.starts_with("get.");
342: 
343:     let (has_arguments_block, argument_validations) = extract_arguments_blocks(node, source);
344: 
345:     Some(FunctionMeta {
346:         name,
347:         inputs,
348:         outputs,
349:         is_constructor,
350:         is_setter,
351:         is_getter,
352:         has_arguments_block,
353:         argument_validations,
354:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
355:         line: node.start_position().row + 1,
356:         end_line: node.end_position().row + 1,
357:         is_method,
358:         is_abstract,
359:         method_attributes: method_attributes.to_vec(),
360:     })
361: }

397: /// Extract input argument names from a function definition.
398: fn extract_function_inputs(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<String> {
399:     let mut names = Vec::new();
400:     let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
401: 
402:     for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
403:         if child.kind() == "function_arguments" {
404:             let mut inner = child.walk();
405:             for param in child.children(&mut inner) {
406:                 match param.kind() {
407:                     "identifier" => {
408:                         names.push(node_text(param, source).to_string());
409:                     }
410:                     "ignored_argument" => {
411:                         names.push("~".to_string());
412:                     }
413:                     _ => {}
414:                 }
415:             }
416:             break;
417:         }
418:     }
419: 
420:     names
421: }
422: 
423: /// Extract output argument names from a function definition.
424: fn extract_function_outputs(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<String> {
425:     let mut names = Vec::new();
426:     let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
427: 
428:     for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
429:         if child.kind() == "function_output" {
430:             let mut inner = child.walk();
431:             for out_child in child.children(&mut inner) {
432:                 match out_child.kind() {
433:                     "identifier" => {
434:                         names.push(node_text(out_child, source).to_string());
435:                     }
436:                     "ignored_argument" => {
437:                         names.push("~".to_string());
438:                     }
439:                     "multioutput_variable" => {
440:                         let mut mv_cursor = out_child.walk();
441:                         for mv_child in out_child.children(&mut mv_cursor) {
442:                             match mv_child.kind() {
443:                                 "identifier" => {
444:                                     names.push(node_text(mv_child, source).to_string());
445:                                 }
446:                                 "ignored_argument" => {
447:                                     names.push("~".to_string());
448:                                 }
449:                                 _ => {}
450:                             }
451:                         }
452:                     }
453:                     _ => {}
454:                 }
455:             }
456:             break;
457:         }
458:     }
459: 
460:     names
461: }

463: /// Extract `arguments` validation blocks from within a function definition.
464: ///
465: /// Returns `(has_arguments_block, validations)`.
466: fn extract_arguments_blocks(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> (bool, Vec<ArgValidation>) {
467:     let mut validations = Vec::new();
468:     let mut found = false;
469: 
470:     let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
471:     for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
472:         if child.kind() == "arguments_statement" {
473:             found = true;
474:             // Each `property` child inside the arguments block describes one argument.
475:             let mut inner = child.walk();
476:             for arg_child in child.children(&mut inner) {
477:                 if arg_child.kind() == "property" {
478:                     if let Some(validation) = extract_arg_validation(arg_child, source) {
479:                         validations.push(validation);
480:                     }
481:                 }
482:             }
483:         }
484:     }
485: 
486:     (found, validations)
487: }

489: /// Extract a single argument validation entry from a `property` node inside
490: /// an `arguments` block.
491: fn extract_arg_validation(prop_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<ArgValidation> {
492:     let name = prop_node
493:         .child_by_field_name("name")
494:         .or_else(|| find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "identifier"))
495:         .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string())?;
496: 
497:     let dimensions =
498:         find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "dimensions").map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string());
499: 
500:     // Type constraint: bare identifier after dimensions (not the name).
501:     let type_constraint = extract_type_constraint(prop_node, source, &name);
502: 
503:     let validators = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "validation_functions")
504:         .map(|vf| {
505:             let mut v = Vec::new();
506:             let mut vc = vf.walk();
507:             for vchild in vf.children(&mut vc) {
508:                 if vchild.kind() == "identifier" {
509:                     v.push(node_text(vchild, source).to_string());
510:                 }
511:             }
512:             v
513:         })
514:         .unwrap_or_default();
515: 
516:     let default_value = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "default_value").map(|dv| {
517:         // The actual expression is the child(ren) after `=`.
518:         // Use the full text, trimming the leading `=` if present.
519:         let text = node_text(dv, source).trim().to_string();
520:         let text = text.strip_prefix('=').unwrap_or(&text).trim().to_string();
521:         text
522:     });
523: 
524:     Some(ArgValidation {
525:         name,
526:         dimensions,
527:         type_constraint,
528:         validators,
529:         default_value,
530:     })
531: }
532: 
533: /// Extract the type constraint from a property node.
534: ///
535: /// In MATLAB, the property syntax is: `name (dims) type {validators} = default`.
536: /// The type is a bare identifier (or `property_name` for dotted names)
537: /// that appears after dimensions but before validation_functions/default_value.
538: fn extract_type_constraint(prop_node: Node, source: &str, prop_name: &str) -> Option<String> {
539:     let mut cursor = prop_node.walk();
540:     let mut past_name = false;
541:     let mut past_dims = false;
542: 
543:     for child in prop_node.children(&mut cursor) {
544:         let kind = child.kind();
545: 
546:         // Skip the name identifier.
547:         if !past_name {
548:             if kind == "identifier" || kind == "property_name" {
549:                 let text = node_text(child, source);
550:                 if text == prop_name {
551:                     past_name = true;
552:                     continue;
553:                 }
554:             }
555:             continue;
556:         }
557: 
558:         // Skip dimensions.
559:         if kind == "dimensions" {
560:             past_dims = true;
561:             continue;
562:         }
563: 
564:         // If we haven't seen dimensions yet and we encounter an identifier,
565:         // it could still be the type (dimensions are optional).
566:         if !past_dims && kind == "dimensions" {
567:             continue;
568:         }
569: 
570:         // The type constraint is the first identifier/property_name after
571:         // the property name (and optional dimensions).
572:         if kind == "identifier" || kind == "property_name" {
573:             return Some(node_text(child, source).to_string());
574:         }
575: 
576:         // If we hit validation_functions or default_value, no type was specified.
577:         if kind == "validation_functions" || kind == "default_value" || kind == "=" {
578:             return None;
579:         }
580:     }
581: 
582:     None
583: }

638: /// Extract class metadata from a `class_definition` node.
639: fn extract_class_meta(class_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<ClassMeta> {
640:     let name_node = class_node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
641:     let class_name = node_text(name_node, source).to_string();
642: 
643:     // Superclasses.
644:     let superclasses = find_first_child_of_kind(class_node, "superclasses")
645:         .map(|sc| {
646:             let mut names = Vec::new();
647:             let mut cursor = sc.walk();
648:             for child in sc.children(&mut cursor) {
649:                 match child.kind() {
650:                     "identifier" | "property_name" => {
651:                         names.push(node_text(child, source).to_string());
652:                     }
653:                     _ => {}
654:                 }
655:             }
656:             names
657:         })
658:         .unwrap_or_default();
659: 
660:     // Class-level attributes.
661:     let attributes = find_first_child_of_kind(class_node, "attributes")
662:         .map(|a| extract_attributes(a, source))
663:         .unwrap_or_default();
664: 
665:     // Collect section blocks.
666:     let mut properties_blocks = Vec::new();
667:     let mut methods_blocks = Vec::new();
668:     let mut events_blocks = Vec::new();
669:     let mut enumeration_blocks = Vec::new();
670: 
671:     let mut cursor = class_node.walk();
672:     for child in class_node.children(&mut cursor) {
673:         match child.kind() {
674:             "properties" => {
675:                 properties_blocks.push(extract_properties_block(child, source));
676:             }
677:             "methods" => {
678:                 methods_blocks.push(extract_methods_block(child, source, &class_name));
679:             }
680:             "events" => {
681:                 events_blocks.push(extract_events_block(child, source));
682:             }
683:             "enumeration" => {
684:                 enumeration_blocks.push(extract_enumeration_block(child, source));
685:             }
686:             _ => {}
687:         }
688:     }
689: 
690:     Some(ClassMeta {
691:         name: class_name,
692:         superclasses,
693:         attributes,
694:         properties_blocks,
695:         methods_blocks,
696:         events_blocks,
697:         enumeration_blocks,
698:         byte_range: class_node.start_byte()..class_node.end_byte(),
699:         line: class_node.start_position().row + 1,
700:     })
701: }

703: /// Extract a `properties ... end` block.
704: fn extract_properties_block(props_node: Node, source: &str) -> PropertiesBlockMeta {
705:     let attributes = find_first_child_of_kind(props_node, "attributes")
706:         .map(|a| extract_attributes(a, source))
707:         .unwrap_or_default();
708: 
709:     let mut properties = Vec::new();
710:     let mut cursor = props_node.walk();
711:     for child in props_node.children(&mut cursor) {
712:         if child.kind() == "property" {
713:             if let Some(pm) = extract_property_meta(child, source) {
714:                 properties.push(pm);
715:             }
716:         }
717:     }
718: 
719:     PropertiesBlockMeta {
720:         attributes,
721:         properties,
722:     }
723: }

725: /// Extract a `methods ... end` block.
726: fn extract_methods_block(methods_node: Node, source: &str, class_name: &str) -> MethodsBlockMeta {
727:     let block_attributes = find_first_child_of_kind(methods_node, "attributes")
728:         .map(|a| extract_attributes(a, source))
729:         .unwrap_or_default();
730: 
731:     let mut methods = Vec::new();
732:     let mut cursor = methods_node.walk();
733:     for child in methods_node.children(&mut cursor) {
734:         match child.kind() {
735:             "function_definition" => {
736:                 if let Some(fm) = extract_function_meta(
737:                     child,
738:                     source,
